I have installed several types of vent covers over the years and most required drilling 4 small holes to mount the brackets. This one touts "no drilling", which I thought might be better. That is before I saw how much lap sealant was over and around the 4 screws that had to be removed then reinstalled thru the brackets. This is typical on RV roofs around anything mounted there.  If you don't have experience removing lap sealant, it is one of the hardest and stickiest sealants on earth. It makes silicone look like child's play! Just removing it from around the 4 screws on one vent pretty much used up my hand strength for the day. This is all MUCH more labor intensive than drilling 4 small holes, trust me!

While looking for a vent cover for my Fan-Tastic kitchen vent, I found this one to be quite pricy but thought, "it must be worth it because it is made by the same manufacturer as the vent that it will be covering." Well I read through the reviews and found one that stated that it wouldn't allow the vent to open fully. I figured that maybe they didn't install it properly or something to that nature. As it turns out, they were correct! It stops the vent from opening about 2 inches shy of wide open. I guess that the only good thing that that same person did not know is that the motor that opens and closes the vent lid is not setup to operate on a set of limit switches. It in fact opens and closes until it reaches its limit of travel and then the motor will "amp out" and shut off. Because of this, you don't have to worry about damaging anything and it will work just fine. There may be some nay sayers out there that believe that the lid must open all of the way to achieve full flow through the opening but if you do the math and measure the surface area of the screen in front of the fan blades and then the surface area of the opening with the cover installed, you still will have more than enough for the fan to achieve full flow. It has not yet rained sense the install of the cover so I can't comment on how well it works in that scenario, but I will be sure to update my review as soon as it does.

This was purchased after much research. The vendor could save a lot of trouble by simply saying it mounts directly on Fantastic Breeze roof vent fans with very little work. Also, would it kill them to pre-drill/mold the 1/4 holes needed to mount to such a system?

After putting over the roof vent and finding it did in fact 'fit' the mounting tabs already on my RV. I was able to drill four 1/4" holes to line up with the holes in my roof tabs. You could make the arguement that 4 more holes would let insects through. Well since they don't include a screen on the back/vent portion, throw that argument out the window.

After the holes are drilled, the included 1/4" push rivets hold it on nicely. I'm sure it's a hair more work to remove and clean. I usually only take my roof vent cover off 1 or 2 times a year for thorough roof cleaning, so no big deal.

It does include brackets for traditional mounting to the sides of your fan/vent or to it's flange screws. In that second case you would need to reseal, so I always avoid those!

Seriously Fan-Tastic vent people, add a picture to your web page. Add a mount style to your video, showing how your own fan works with this product!
